notes.title: Dev Update #4: Why It's Taking a While
notes.content:
Hi everyone, David here again! Believe it or not, it's almost been a year since I revealed We Harvest Shadows to the world at gamescom 2024. It honestly bums me out a bit because I had been working on this game for about three years prior to the announcement, and I'm realizing there's a [i][b]lot[/b][/i] left to do. I really wanted the game to be out by now, but unfortunately I need more time. I wanted to explain the situation, because ultimately it all comes back to one big decision I made a while back.

So, the demo came out, it was a hit, my dreams were coming true, and I was super grateful for that. But I really didn't know if the game would garner any attention before that moment. My other games and online school were barely making money, so we were withdrawing tens of thousands of dollars from my retirement account. It was a pretty stressful time... and luckily, the gamble paid off. My game almost has 300,000 wishlists now. THANK YOU! 🙏

Even with the insane hours and money I poured into the demo, there were still critical bugs and performance issues we could not figure out (the demo currently runs at a blazing 10 FPS on Steam Deck). It took three years to get an imperfect demo released, and I knew the full game would have to be better in every conceivable way. I desperately did not want to release a half-finished, bug-ridden game. There's a famous quote that describes the situation: "I didn't come this far to only come this far."

I was also super burnt out. This was by far the biggest, most ambitious game I could ever imagine making, and I just didn't have a lot of gas left in the tank. I needed help. [b]Or[/b] I needed to compromise the full vision of the game, and hope players wouldn't be too disappointed. I really didn't like the idea of Early Access because the story and ending are so important to the whole game... I wanted it to feel like a complete experience on day one.

Kickstarter was considered, but I talked to other devs who ran successful campaigns and they convinced me it wasn't ideal. It would hurt my launch momentum due to Steam keys not helping the algorithm, it would take a lot of time to fulfill rewards (instead of working on the full game), and it still wouldn't be enough money to hire the right people. It made more sense to keep scraping by with my own retirement funds.

So anyway, it eventually boiled down to a big crossroads:

[olist]
[*] I use the rest of my retirement and finish the game as fast as possible. I would be happy with a "Mostly Positive" from player reviews on Steam in that case.
[*] I go with my dream publisher, get a large budget, work with the best people I'd always wanted to work with, and make this the best version of itself possible... but I would need to accept that it would take much longer to finish.
[/olist]
As you can probably tell, I went with option 2! And I don't have any regrets! Having enough funding to hire talented people has made this so much more enjoyable for me. It means we can update the engine and rendering pipeline so that a simultaneous, optimized PC/console launch is possible. It means the game will be the most cinematic, gorgeous, memorable experience I always wanted it to be. Speaking of talented people, check out this sweet animation made by Bradley P.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/65b4cf0d36a67dfa157001f946032fccaa5c04cc.gif[/img]

So thank you for your patience! We are making progress. Here is the first screenshot of the game with a new environment, rendering pipeline, weather system, and much more. I'm so excited for the future, and to make this game the best it can be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/10ed354b04f83213c83ae7f99f9cb915aea3454e.jpg[/img]

Sincerely,
David

notes.title: Dev Update #3: Trying Something New with Horror
notes.content:
Hi everyone, David here with a new update. There are so many cool things happening with [i]We Harvest Shadows[/i], but unfortunately I can't share anything yet. BUT just know that we're working hard and some amazing things are happening that will make this the best game I could have envisioned. I need more time though, but the wait will be worth it.

I wanted to talk about my goals for the horror and atmosphere in [i]We Harvest Shadows[/i]. I always wanted this to be a story and character focused game, but the psychological horror elements are key to Garrett's journey. His inner-demons and greatest fears physically manifest on this farm (but [i]why[/i] does that happen? You'll have to play and find out 😉)

I always wanted this game to be a totally different type of horror experience. A24 films have popularized a new subgenre called neo-horror (and I love those films), so I thought "why can't there be a neo-horror game?" I really think gamers want something new when it comes to horror, so I'm trying to avoid as many clichés as possible.

So first off, I play a lot of indie horror games, and I watch a lot of horror movies. I personally am tired of death cults, zombies, demons, etc. Not to crap on those games, but they don't really scare me much. Nowadays, I'm more interested in why the cursed video tape in [i]The Ring[/i] is so terrifying, even without the typical gore or jump scares.

Do you know what truly scares me? Feeling totally alone in a forest, and suddenly seeing a normal face hide behind a tree. Disfigured creatures which look human but [b]aren't[/b] really scare me. I think catching a glimpse of something you can't make quite make out in the darkness is the scariest thing of all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/a1f2a7f3493b1514b8d8e59e45227805bc3bb454.gif[/img]

Most of the great horror films like [i]The Shining[/i] or [i]Hereditary[/i] are very restrained or "slow burn". There's not really much horror in finally seeing the monster that's following you (that's actually the release), but it's in the build-up and the tension. That's also because the scariest thing to [b]you[/b] is what your mind imagines when it fills in the blanks.

That doesn't mean you can't have any payoff or release in a horror game... that would be just boring. But I really want [i]We Harvest Shadows[/i] to be an elevated, beautiful type of horror game which takes it time and marinates in the atmosphere. I want the monsters and entities to look like something you've never seen before. I want them to be narratively rich and to symbolize the deep trauma that Garrett's going through. You can probably guess that Silent Hill is a huge inspiration for me. It's those creature designs and industrial soundscapes which really sell the horror in those games. It's almost pure atmosphere!

Below is my mood board I'm using as inspiration. Some of the sculptures are actually beautiful but still unsettling. There's lots of nature-themed materials. I really love these examples:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/043abd3e0af7b007459d7e3ff639218b129bea0c.jpg[/img]

From a gameplay perspective, we have an advanced dynamic horror system that takes into account lots of different factors. There will be dozens of unique events, and every playthrough will be different. Some entities are more dangerous than others, but even I can't know what exactly will happen to you when the sun sets and the forest darkens.

Now, this does mean that players who typically like sudden jump scares  or tons of gore will probably be disappointed in this game, and I'm totally OK with that. I want this game to feel unique and that means taking a risk. I do however want this game to as scary as possible, but it might not be exactly what you're expecting... which can be pretty scary on its own!

If you loved the gameplay in the demo but didn't like the horror elements, the good news is that there will be an "endless mode" which allows you to customize those types of things since it's more of a sandbox mode than the story mode. I want to give players the choice!

I hope this all made sense, and I'm excited to keep working on the game and share more with you soon. Thanks for the support, and until then, watch your back the next time you find yourself in a dark forest.

Sincerely,
David

notes.title: Dev Update #2: What's Your Favorite Fishing System?
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

David here, letting you know that development is going swimmingly for [i]We Harvest Shadows[/i]. I wanted to show off some of the new fishing system, but I also would love to get your feedback on the kind of fishing systems from other games [i][b]you[/b][/i] love. I really don't know the best direction to take this in, so some ideas would be really appreciated.

[h1]First off, when is this game coming out?[/h1]

I get this question a lot, and I wanted to let you know that there is [i][b]no official release date yet[/b][/i]. I'm sorry that it's a disappointing non-answer, but I'm also grateful that people love the demo so much and want the full game ASAP. However, if I released this game as it stands, it seriously would not be fun or enjoyable. I want to make sure it's as good, fulfilling, and bug-free as possible, so I need more time (at least a year). I hope you understand, but the wait will be worth it. I'll try my best to keep you updated here on Steam, and you could always sign up for the [url=https://www.weharvestshadows.com/newsletter]no-spam newsletter[/url] on the website where big announcements get, uh, announced. Thank you so much for your support!

[h1]The Fishing Rod[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/0c02ac8d282e1e093068ad6aac846e860d3db93f.gif[/img]

I went back and forth on this a lot, but I feel like this "anti-cozy" farming game wouldn't be complete without a fishing system of some kind. We decided to bite the bullet and go for it, and it's really fun so far! There will be upgradeable rods with increased chances to get rarer, more valuable fish, and certain fish will only be found in certain bodies of water. Like most gameplay aspects in this game, you can sell the fish and use the funds to build up your farm.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/526efd8dbeb5385e4491a37ad96607577c4ec5bf.gif[/img]

There are so many little things that go into a game to make it feel good and satisfying. There's a lot of animation and sound work that has already gone into it, and the above GIF shows a physics tests we're doing when a fish is caught and they flounder around.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/65c6283c83716b7f3aadbe2fb809dff6cfd7b45d.jpg[/img]

I also made a water cooler that can carry the fish around so you can throw them in the trailer to sell. And of course, since this is [i]We Harvest Shadows[/i] and things tend to get a bit eerie, expect the unexpected too.

[h1]I need your help[/h1]

I've done a ton of research and note taking on my favorite fishing systems in games. I grew up playing a lot of Zelda Ocarina of Time fishing, which was pretty relaxed and simple, but I'm also drawn to more complex systems. My question to you is: [b]what are your favorite fishing systems from all of video games?[/b] Maybe you like it super simple like Minecraft, or do you like it a bit more in-depth like Stardew Valley or Dredge? Let me know what you think in the comments, it would really help me a lot.

Thank you for the support! I'll keep plugging away, and I'll do my best to keep you informed on development. Take care everyone.

notes.title: Dev Update #1: ATV and Exploration
notes.content:
Hey everyone, I wanted to give you an update on [i]We Harvest Shadows[/i] and let you know that [i][b]so many cool things are happening[/b][/i]. I can't go into specifics yet, but if there was a best case scenario for finding a great partner to make the game fantastic, then it's (probably) happening.

At first, I was wondering if I should make the game "decent" and get it done fast, but now I've decided that I want to make it the best version of itself, which means I'll need more time and a publisher to make it happen. I think some people were hoping to play the full game really soon, but I'm humbly asking for more time as we work on the full version and make it an unforgettable gaming experience. I'm sorry for the long wait, but it will be worth it. I would be heartbroken if I released a buggy, unoptimized mess, and it took away from the full story and experience. Thanks for your patience!

Anyways, we're working hard and making progress. Last week I worked on new crops and the opening cinematic, and my lead programmer Connor fixed a ton of bugs. I also wanted to show you a really fun tool for the player... the All-Terrain Vehicle, or ATV!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/5344e22d15bbe48b63f01d8b1b6c6b402bcad8bb.gif[/img]

A big part of the mid/end game will be exploring the vast property near your house, and uncovering the history and secrets of this land you live on. Who lived here? Why is it abandoned? Why is there a sinister presence that emerges at night? It's this type of exploration and storytelling that made me fall in love with games in the first place. There will also be lots of secrets to uncover for the perceptive, eagle-eyed player!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/01ff98f839ae75e248d832079b8b3cd78c9456ed.jpg[/img]

You'll also be able to loot each spot and find valuable items, which is why your ATV has a trailer attached to it. You just drop your items in the back and unload them at your house! Also, your map will keep track of each location, telling you if you've cleared an area and found every secret. I really love the Silent Hill 2 map system, so it will probably something like that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157714/a162a3c1e892cd3337c33ecc985608b237aa56dd.gif[/img]

I won't spoil all the locations, but it's over a square mile of places to explore, laid out by hand. The ATV makes it much more fun to find all these places and get to them quickly, and of course, you can upgrade the ATV over time and enhance the storage capacity, speed, and add other cool features.

Thanks for your support of WHS! I'm at 225,000 wishlists now which is unbelievable. I'm excited to make a game that lives up to your expectations. I think you'll agree the wait will be worth it. Until then, take care, and consider subscribing to the [url=https://www.weharvestshadows.com/newsletter]WHS newsletter on my website[/url]. Thanks again everyone!

- David
